values.name: Rann of Kutch
values.location: Dhordo and the Great Rann visitor area, Kutch, Gujarat
values.description: The Great Rann is a seasonal salt landscape in northern Kutch. Dhordo provides access to the White Rann, while Kalo Dungar offers elevated views over the surrounding region.
values.seasonal_note: The white salt surface depends on weather and water conditions; monsoon conditions can change access and appearance. Permit requirements apply.

records.notes: Months represent recommended dry-season travel, not an asserted legal closure calendar.

values.name: White Rann near Dhordo
values.entry_fee: Published adult White Rann permit INR100; vehicle permit and optional activities extra; confirm current permit tariff
values.description: The White Rann near Dhordo is a seasonal salt-flat viewing destination, commonly visited around sunset and full-moon periods.
values.best_time_note: A local published day plan allocates16:30-19:00 before dinner; stored2.5 hours is that visit allowance, not opening hours. Accessibility guide reports assisted access at the viewing area but uneven salt crust beyond it. Do not infer independent wheelchair access across the flats. Permit/seasonal access must be checked.
values.source: Gujarat Tourism; Google Maps; local operators

records.notes: Selected mapped attraction, archived pages/rann-white-selected.json. Permit source is a tour-operator published exclusion, not a successfully retrieved official current tariff; official portal unavailable during research. Price is provisional representative evidence, no guessed vehicle split.

values.name: Kalo Dungar
values.entry_fee: No viewpoint admission charge; local transport/parking and applicable permits separate
values.description: Kalo Dungar is Kutch's highest hill, with views across the Great Rann and a Dattatreya temple near the summit.
values.best_time_note: Published visit guidance suggests1-2 hours. IRCTC notes over1km uphill from bus parking and limited local transfer options; wheelchair access to the final viewpoint is unverified. Road routes are approach routes, not proof of step-free summit access.
values.source: Gujarat Tourism; OpenStreetMap; IRCTC; regional guide

records.notes: 1.5 hours is midpoint of published1-2 hour guidance, which includes hill approach; may overlap road approach time. No clock opening/closing invented for daylight access.
